{"id":"persona-5s4b.93","title":"did:key and GPG identities are issued under the ssh.local trust domain","description":"Trust-domain namespace collision across three attestors of differing provenance.

persona-attestors/src/did_key.rs:70 and persona-attestors/src/gpg.rs:89 both hard-code TrustDomain::SshLocal:
    SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::SshLocal, format!("did/{short}"))
    SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::SshLocal, format!("gpg/{short_fp}"))
persona-attestors/src/ssh.rs issues under the same domain. Meanwhile TrustDomain::PgpLocal and TrustDomain::PersonalDid(String) (persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:39,48) exist for exactly these two cases and have no construction site anywhere outside spiffe_id.rs and its tests. SPEC-HIA documents personal.{did} and pgp.local as distinct domains.

CONSEQUENCE: the trust domain is the coarse-grained authorization handle - a relying party writing "trust spiffe://ssh.local/*" intends to trust locally enrolled SSH keys and instead also trusts anything in the GPG keyring and anything named in the PERSONA_DID_KEYS environment variable. The last of those is the weakest possible source: did_key.rs:50-52 reads PERSONA_DID_KEYS from the environment and performs no verification that the user controls the corresponding private key, so setting one env var mints an identity in the SSH trust domain. Separating the domains lets an RP decline did:key without declining SSH.

Not exploitable as a bypass on its own - the path prefixes (did/, gpg/, and the ssh attestors own prefix) do differ, so an RP matching full paths is unaffected. It matters for RPs matching on trust domain, which is the intended granularity.

Fix direction: use TrustDomain::PersonalDid(did) in did_key.rs and TrustDomain::PgpLocal in gpg.rs.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:52.034016844Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:52.034016844Z","labels":["crypto","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.93","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:52.053468417Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"design":"BLOCKED as written. Investigated 2026-09-14 while closing the GPG cluster; do not implement the stated fix direction without resolving these first.

1. FLIPPING THE CONSTANT BREAKS ISSUANCE. personad/src/main.rs:37 seeds exactly one trust bundle: bundles.upsert(TrustBundle::local(TrustDomain::SshLocal, &signer)). Nothing seeds pgp.local or personal.*. persona-attestors/tests/unix_account_live.rs:103-108 already asserts this coupling in so many words -- 'personad seeds a trust bundle only for ssh.local, so a candidate under any other domain would fail the daemon own ValidateJWTSVID'. So changing SelfAssertedDomain::SshLocal to PgpLocal in gpg.rs would move GPG identities into a domain with no bundle and no verifier, i.e. silently stop them working rather than separating them.

2. SEEDING pgp.local WITH THE SAME SIGNER IS COSMETIC. The point of the split (per the bead) is that an RP matching on trust domain can decline GPG without declining SSH. If personad seeds both domains from the same SvidSigner key, one key signs both and an RP gains no cryptographic separation -- only a label it must trust the daemon to apply honestly. Real separation needs a key per domain, which is a trust-model decision for Mark, not an attestor edit.

3. THE did:key HALF DOES NOT WORK AS WRITTEN AT ALL. The fix direction says use TrustDomain::PersonalDid(did). TrustDomain Display renders that variant as 'personal.{did}' (persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:57), so a did:key value yields the authority 'personal.did:key:z6Mk...'. That is a URI authority containing colons, which parse as a port separator -- not a valid SPIFFE trust domain. Whatever goes in PersonalDid must be a bare label, so the did cannot be used directly. Note also persona-5s4b.37: PersonalDid round-trips ambiguously against OrgOidc, so that variant needs .37 settled first.

SUGGESTED ORDER: settle .37 (trust-domain namespace), then decide the per-domain-key question, then move the attestors. The one-line change in gpg.rs/did_key.rs is the last step, not the first.

The ponytail comments in gpg.rs and did_key.rs name this migration as their upgrade path. Their stated gate -- 'a change that also migrates any enrolled SPIFFE IDs' -- is already satisfied: persona-5s4b.103 established there is no enrollment store anywhere, so nothing is keyed on the current IDs. The real gate is the trust bundle, not enrollment."}
